data.name: Jadirah
data.gender_notes: Jadirah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A woman who tends to her garden and makes it rain, radiating beauty and joy. The name Jadirah carries the meaning “Gardener, rainmaker, radiant one” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Jadirah usually hope their child will grow to embody gardener, rainmaker, radiant one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A woman who nurtures her inner garden and shares her blessings with the world
data.etymology: Jadirah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gardener, rainmaker, radiant one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jadirah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jadirah evokes the image of a woman who is both nurturing and productive. In Islamic culture, gardens are symbols of paradise and acts of cultivation represent the ongoing process of self-improvement, provision for one's family, and a means of connecting with nature. To be Jadirah then, is to be the person who makes things grow, rendering the world a more beautiful and lively place.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jadirah carries deeper spiritual meaning as well, as it refers to an owner of a garden, but not just an owner, it is the one who tends to it and makes it flourish. The role of a gardener is to work with nature to coax life from the earth, and in doing so, one comes to understand the delicate balance and interconnectedness of all creatures. Jadirah embodies the concept of stewardship and service to the Creator, for it is an acknowledgment of the gift of life, and the Grace that makes growth possible. Jadirah reminds us of the importance of being diligent, tending to our spiritual gardens, and nurturing our hearts so they may radiate beauty and joy.
